rule: GOAL: Reach the exit before the timer runs out. CONTROLS: Arrows move your character; each press costs one time unit. RULE: The shrinking magenta bar is your remaining move budget, not just decoration. TRAP: Assuming you can wander freely; ignoring the step limit wastes actions and causes failure.

GOAL: Guide the falling ball to land inside the yellow cup gaps. CONTROLS: Arrows move the blue paddle horizontally; space launches the hanging ball. RULE: The ball splits into two on paddle contact, traveling diagonally outward to fill the target zones. TRAP: Assuming balls bounce off cup walls to enter; they actually pass through gaps or hit the floor, requiring precise paddle alignment.

GOAL: Guide the cursor to the exit using only mouse clicks. CONTROLS: Clicking blue blocks shifts the gray boundary; the cursor sticks to this edge. RULE: The cursor moves exactly as the gray region expands or contracts at its current row. TRAP: Assuming clicks move the cursor directly; they actually reshape the terrain, dragging the cursor along the new edge.

GOAL: Collect all marked targets by positioning matching colored cross arms over them. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active cross. Spacebar switches control between the yellow and blue crosses. RULE: A target is collected only when a cross arm of the same color covers it completely. TRAP: Moving the yellow cross away after collecting its targets does not undo progress, but forgetting to switch colors wastes turns.

GOAL: Move the square to the target by clicking specific grid points. CONTROLS: Clicking a coordinate attempts to move the square toward that spot. RULE: The square jumps only as far as its range limit allows in one click. TRAP: Believing you can reach the goal in one click when the range is shorter.

GOAL: Extend both bars to length 26 so their red markers land exactly on the plus signs' centers. CONTROLS: Clicking a bar extends it by 3 units; clicking again retracts it by 3 units. RULE: The plus is fully covered and centered only when the bar length is 26, aligning the marker with the middle row. TRAP: Assuming the marker could hit the center at other lengths; it only aligns at length 26 due to the 3-unit step size.

GOAL: Slide the lower band right to align the key with the wall gap. CONTROLS: Click below the wall to move the lower band right; click above to move the upper band left. RULE: Each click shifts the band four units, requiring five clicks to bridge the twenty-unit gap. TRAP: Assuming the upper band’s leftward shift helps, but only the lower band’s rightward movement matters.

GOAL: Move three pods to their target slots using a push mechanic. CONTROLS: Arrows move the avatar; Space picks up or drops a pod held directly above. RULE: You can only carry one pod at a time; it must sit in the square immediately above you. TRAP: Assuming you can carry a pod horizontally while it is above you; you must drop it if you move away or need to reposition.

GOAL: Align the rotating dial symbols in each column to match the target pattern shown. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between columns; Up and Down arrows rotate the dial in the current column. RULE: The dial cycles through symbols in a fixed order, so choose the shortest rotation path to the target. TRAP: Assuming rotation direction is arbitrary; ignoring the fixed cycle order leads to unnecessary moves and wasted actions.

GOAL: Flip all switches to black to power the plug into the socket. CONTROLS: Clicking a switch toggles its color between gray and black. RULE: The plug only moves when every single switch is set to black. TRAP: Thinking partial matches or alternating patterns would complete the circuit.

GOAL: Align the plus and X shapes to cover all target dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected object; Space cycles to the next object. RULE: Each shape must perfectly overlay its matching colored targets. TRAP: Assuming Space cycles in a fixed order; verify the cursor position before moving.

GOAL: Arrange seven tiles into two rows, matching top constraints to bottom pairs while cycling through a rotating dial. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP rotates the current tile forward through its sequence; DOWN rotates backward. RULE: Each top pair dictates specific bottom tiles; the dial cycles through all seven classes, so find the shortest rotation distance. TRAP: Assuming a fixed starting position wastes actions; probing the full cycle first reveals the optimal path for every slot.

GOAL: Reach the exit in three moves while avoiding the stationary red guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Guards only dash horizontally along their own row, leaving vertical paths safe. TRAP: Assuming guards attack from any direction wastes time; walking straight past them vertically is safe.

GOAL: Transform the input row into the output row by applying pair mappings to segmented glyph chunks. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor and rotated the glyph in the active slot to cycle through possible shapes. RULE: Segmentation was unique; each input chunk had exactly one valid mapping to the required output sequence. TRAP: Assuming fixed chunk sizes caused wasted rotations; correct grouping was deduced from the total output length.

GOAL: Cover all red dots by aligning shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows move shapes three cells. Space switches selection. RULE: Shapes must fully cover every dot simultaneously to win. TRAP: Moving one shape first may block paths; plan final positions before moving.

GOAL: Move three keys to specific gaps by raising or lowering water levels in five columns. CONTROLS: Four buttons raise or lower water in adjacent column pairs, creating linked movements. RULE: Keys float on water, so aligning water height with gaps places keys correctly. TRAP: Assuming arrows dictate key direction wasted time; water height alone determines position.

GOAL: Match the target pattern to unlock the plug. CONTROLS: Click boxes to toggle plug direction, switches to set bars, and the ball to launch. RULE: The plug moves in the active direction only if the switch pattern matches the goal. TRAP: Thinking the ball click fixes errors; it only executes the move, reverting if the pattern is wrong.

ESTABLISHED: Extending the arm pushes overlapping blocks along the arm's axis. FAILED: Assuming blocks stay static during arm movement; ignoring slot boundary limits. GOAL IS NOT: Simply extending the arm to touch a target without managing block positions. CONTROLS: Left/Right retracts/extends arm; Up/Down moves player and arm between vertical slots.

GOAL: Match the bottom shapes to the top targets by cycling through hidden pairs. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shifted the shape in the active slot through its specific transformation chain. RULE: Each shape followed a fixed S-to-P-to-Y sequence, requiring multiple presses to reach the correct yellow state. TRAP: Assuming one press fixed a slot wasted moves; you had to cycle through the intermediate purple shape to land on yellow.

GOAL: Reach the exit by capturing all guards without being dashed. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step in that direction. RULE: Guards dash only if you stand directly in front of their face; approach from the side or back to capture safely. TRAP: Assuming guards attack any adjacent square wastes time; they ignore threats from behind or perpendicular angles.

GOAL: Match specific input and output shapes for each tile by cycling through two separate shape sequences. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor; pressing up or down rotated the current tile’s shape through its color-specific cycle. RULE: Input and output tiles followed independent seven-shape loops, requiring separate calculations for each side of a tile. TRAP: Assuming a single shared cycle for all tiles caused initial confusion; recognizing distinct input and output sequences was essential.

GOAL: Stack all three blocks in one slot, ordered red, blue, black, against the wall. CONTROLS: Arrows move your arm to grab, lift, or push blocks into different vertical slots. RULE: Blocks stack in the order you push them, so arrange them left-to-right before lifting. TRAP: Assuming you can reorder blocks while they are stacked; you must set the order before combining them.

GOAL: Place colored tiles into the four slots in the exact sequence shown by the outline bar at the top. CONTROLS: Click a tile from the bottom supply row to select it, then click a middle slot to insert it. RULE: The top bar displays the strict left-to-right order required for the slots, acting as the visual key. TRAP: Assuming any fill order works wastes steps; the supply tiles cannot be reused once placed.

GOAL: Guide the white head so the straight rope passes through the ring, not just touching it. CONTROLS: Clicking moves the selected node; the tail stays fixed unless unlocked by specific interactions. RULE: The rope remains a single straight segment connecting head and tail at all times. TRAP: Assuming the ring is a solid obstacle to avoid rather than a target for alignment.

GOAL: Rotate the ring so the yellow tile lands exactly on the dashed marker slot. CONTROLS: The red arrow shifts all tiles one step counterclockwise along the perimeter. RULE: The yellow tile starts five positions away, requiring exactly five red clicks to align it. TRAP: Assuming the dashed line was a static indicator rather than the specific target position for the yellow tile.

GOAL: Turn the fourth grid's ring entirely blue to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click any blue tile in a grid to rotate that grid's outer ring one step clockwise. RULE: Only the highlighted fourth grid affects the win condition; ignore the other three grids. TRAP: Believing the center red square is clickable or interactive; clicking it does nothing, wasting moves.

GOAL: Shrink the large tool tip to fit through the narrow notch. CONTROLS: Click diamond patterns to toggle tip size; use arrows to move the tool. RULE: Pressing the four-cell diamond pattern shrinks the tip from four cells wide to two. TRAP: Assuming the tip stays large; failing to shrink it blocks passage through the narrow gap.

GOAL: Move all pegs to the bottom-right corner. CONTROLS: Click a peg to see valid jumps, then click the landing spot to move. RULE: Pegs jump over adjacent neighbors into empty spaces. TRAP: Believing diagonal jumps were allowed; only straight lines work.

GOAL: Match the grid colors to the hidden hubs' patterns. CONTROLS: Click hubs to rotate their view; click tiles to toggle colors. RULE: Each hub defines the correct colors for its surrounding eight tiles. TRAP: Assuming hubs only show their own color, ignoring that they dictate neighbor states.

GOAL: Place seven colored tiles into two boxes to form a specific color sequence. CONTROLS: Click tiles to swap their positions; press space to check the arrangement. RULE: The correct order follows the physical flow path, not just left-to-right reading. TRAP: Assuming tiles fill sequentially from the start ignores that downstream slots must be filled before upstream ones.

GOAL: Pass the large tip through a narrow collar to reach the handle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the arm; keypad clicks shrink the tip. RULE: Shrinking the tip to two-by-two units allows it to fit through the two-unit wide gap. TRAP: Assuming the large tip can pass through the opening by moving it precisely; it must be shrunk first.

GOAL: Rotate two yellow markers to align with the dashed target tiles. CONTROLS: Red and green buttons rotate the top ring or specific rows clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Each rotation shifts tiles one step; yellow markers are identical, so either can occupy a target. TRAP: Assuming row rotations only affect that row; they actually shift tiles shared with the central ring, altering global positions unexpectedly.

GOAL: Fill seven red and side slots to match the top letter sequence. CONTROLS: Click bottom tiles to pick them up, then click empty slots to place them. Press space to verify the solution. RULE: Read slots left to right, but when a pipe connects to a side box, insert that box's slots into the sequence at the pipe's position. TRAP: Assuming side boxes are read separately after the main row; they must be interleaved exactly where the pipe connects.

GOAL: Move the active block into the frame. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected block; clicking swaps control between blocks. RULE: The white dot marks the controllable block; only it can enter the target frame. TRAP: Assuming arrows always control the first block; ignoring the click-to-switch mechanic caused wasted pushes.

GOAL: Connect the red and green boxes by placing a pipe marker, then fill all slots to match the top sequence. CONTROLS: Click a bottom tile to select it, then click a gray slot to place it. Press space to check the solution. RULE: The pipe must sit directly above the green box to link them, fixing its position in the sequence. TRAP: Assuming the pipe is just another tile to fill a slot, rather than the connector defining the reading order.

GOAL: Move the yellow and orange tiles to their specific target slots on the opposite loops. CONTROLS: Four buttons rotate the left and right rings clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: The loops share a single crossing cell, requiring tiles to pass through to switch sides. TRAP: Assuming rings move independently ignores the shared cell bottleneck, trapping tiles on one side.

GOAL: Match the grid pattern to the hub colors. CONTROLS: Click tiles to toggle their state. RULE: White pixels mean Orange; gray pixels mean Red. TRAP: Assuming gray meant Orange because it looked similar to the center.

GOAL: Fit the block into the box by matching its shape to the socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; use the action to rotate or flip it. RULE: The legend shows the block’s current orientation; align it with the box’s keyhole. TRAP: Assuming the block only moves; ignoring that the shape itself must be transformed to fit.

GOAL: Build a sequence matching the top row using red slots and a blue box. CONTROLS: Click tiles to place them in slots; press space to check the solution. RULE: Pipes repeat the entire blue box contents between surrounding red tiles. TRAP: Assuming pipes read only adjacent tiles; they actually duplicate the full blue sequence, requiring specific spacing.

GOAL: Fill colored boxes to match a top sequence by using red box pipes to select reading order. CONTROLS: Click tiles to place; Space to confirm. RULE: Red box pipes determine which colored box reads next, grouping three tiles per box. TRAP: Assuming pipes fill colored boxes directly wastes turns; they only trigger reading order for solid tiles.

ESTABLISHED: Two blocks start at the bottom of separate maze arms. Moves are mirrored horizontally. FAILED: Trying to exit the maze or fill it completely. Ignoring the painting mechanic in initial searches. GOAL IS NOT: Leaving the maze boundaries. Filling the entire area with color. Reaching the absolute top corners specifically. CONTROLS: Input moves both blocks simultaneously; one moves horizontally opposite to the other. Previous positions turn black, blocking future paths.

GOAL: Match every tile to its hub’s center color for whites, and the remaining color for grays. CONTROLS: Click tiles to cycle their colors toward the required hue. RULE: White tiles take the hub’s center color; gray tiles take the other color. TRAP: Assuming gray maps to the base color; it actually maps to the third, non-hub color.

GOAL: Place items in three boxes to force the green box's middle item to land on the yellow target in the final sequence. CONTROLS: Click supply items to select, then click empty slots to place them. Press space to trigger the sequence and check the result. RULE: Each box's middle slot is a pipe that outputs all its items consecutively into the main sequence. TRAP: Assuming pipe order doesn't matter. Misplacing pipes breaks the chain, causing green items to land in wrong positions instead of the target.

GOAL: Guide the battery along the wire to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the battery; clicks activate connectors. RULE: The battery must follow the continuous wire path from start to finish. TRAP: Trying to jump directly to the endpoint ignores the wire’s constraint, wasting time.

GOAL: Navigate two blocks from the bottom arms through the central wedge to the top corridor. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both blocks simultaneously; inputs are mirrored horizontally across the center axis. RULE: Blocks must reach the designated exit zone at the top of the maze to complete the level. TRAP: Believing blocks can merge or pass through each other; they occupy distinct cells, so overlapping paths are invalid.

ESTABLISHED: SPACE replays a ghost of the previous run. The ghost moves down the left corridor and stops at the red block. FAILED: Pressing SPACE repeatedly or moving elsewhere before pressing it. The ghost never passes the block or changes path. GOAL IS NOT: Passing the block with the current player. The ghost cannot break the barrier. CONTROLS: SPACE records and replays. Arrows move the player. The block stays fixed.

GOAL: Reach the dock with the shape in the correct state before energy runs out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; stepping on the cross cycles the shape. RULE: The ring restores full energy, allowing a longer route to align the shape correctly. TRAP: Assuming the cross cycles instantly; you must pass over it twice to reach the target state.

GOAL: Align two specific tiles to marked target spots by sliding them along connected loops. CONTROLS: Click green arrows to shift tiles right or up; click red arrows to shift left or down. RULE: Tiles travel on continuous paths, transferring between the horizontal and vertical loops only at four specific intersection points. TRAP: Assuming the loops are separate grids; ignoring the intersection transfers makes the puzzle unsolvable.

GOAL: Move the two yellow tiles into the two yellow marker slots at the ends of the top row. CONTROLS: Click the top arrows to rotate the top row; click the middle arrows to rotate the entire board in a single long loop. RULE: All tiles follow one continuous path, so moving a tile on the loop shifts every other tile along that same path. TRAP: Believing the top row moves independently; rotating the loop also changes the positions of the top-row tiles you are trying to align.

GOAL: Slide the dark block to cover the yellow outline exactly. CONTROLS: Arrows move both blocks simultaneously, but the dark block moves in the opposite direction of the arrow pressed. RULE: Pressing LEFT shifts the dark block RIGHT, while pressing DOWN shifts it DOWN. TRAP: Assuming arrows move the active block directly; you must invert horizontal inputs for the dark block.

GOAL: Guide the knob from the start box to the yellow target block. CONTROLS: Arrows move the knob two pixels per step; clicks rotate red plugs to shift the red bar. RULE: The knob must remain on the dark red pivot block while the red bar rotates to avoid losing contact. TRAP: Moving the knob off the pivot before rotating the bar causes the circuit to break or the knob to fall.

GOAL: Align the yellow plug with the yellow target marker. CONTROLS: Top clicks moved the upper seam left; bottom clicks moved the lower seam right. RULE: The seams moved symmetrically, maintaining a constant distance, so only one could ever align with the fixed target. TRAP: Trying to align both seams simultaneously wasted time, as their fixed separation made this geometrically impossible.

GOAL: Guide the plug into the socket to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug three cells per press; spacebar rotates it. RULE: The red tips must align perfectly with the green pins to connect. TRAP: Assuming small steps wastes moves; remember each arrow press covers three cells.

GOAL: Align five slots to target colors by cycling through a fixed sequence. CONTROLS: Arrows move selection left or right; Up and Down shift the current slot’s color forward or backward in the cycle. RULE: The cycle order is fixed, so counting steps from the current color to the target determines the exact presses needed. TRAP: Assuming Up and Down are interchangeable wastes moves; one direction advances, the other reverses.

GOAL: Align the sliding piston with the target marker on the right. CONTROLS: Click the top bar to shift the piston right; click the bottom bar to shift it left. RULE: The piston moves only when the top and bottom bars are perfectly aligned horizontally. TRAP: Assuming each click moves the piston one step; it actually jumps four columns, causing overshoots.

GOAL: Reach the bottom-right corner by navigating a grid where gray tiles act as walls and white tiles allow movement. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide your piece two spaces in the chosen direction, landing on the next white tile. RULE: You must stop on white tiles; gray tiles block movement, effectively creating a checkerboard path. TRAP: Believing you can stop on gray tiles wastes moves; realize they are impassable barriers forcing longer routes.

GOAL: Drop the puzzle piece into the bottom socket by activating the correct legend slots. CONTROLS: Click legend slots to toggle their vertical and horizontal bars; click the blue button to execute the drop. RULE: The piece drops one grid cell for every fully activated slot, so all five slots must be black to reach the target. TRAP: Mistaking partial activations for full ones; both the vertical and horizontal parts of a slot must be black to count as active.

GOAL: Move the knob from the starting socket to the yellow target by navigating through gray corridors. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the knob; clicking colored plugs toggles blue or red barriers to open new paths. RULE: Barriers only vanish when their matching plug is active; the knob must land exactly on the yellow square to win. TRAP: Assuming the knob can pass through inactive barriers; it stops dead, forcing costly backtracking to toggle the correct plug first.

ESTABLISHED: The block stays fixed at ten rows. Dipping paints specific areas. Rotating changes the dip footprint. Painting persists only where the frame touches the block. FAILED: Rotating to forty-five degrees and dipping did not clear the level. Painting the top half white and bottom half purple with a central hole did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the legend colors exactly as displayed on the side panel. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the frame. Mouse clicks select paint color. Spacebar dips the frame onto the block.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding the patrolling guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per turn. RULE: The guard only moves when you are within four tiles of him. TRAP: Assuming the guard moves every turn causes you to waste time dodging empty space.

GOAL: Fill the first three tanks to their limits while emptying the others. CONTROLS: Clicking a pipe moves one unit of water from the higher tank to the lower one. RULE: Water only flows if the receiving tank has space below its ceiling. TRAP: Assuming you could dump all water into the last tank first; this blocked the flow needed to fill the upper targets.

ESTABLISHED: The boat rises through water channels. It reached the top pool, then the level reset with the boat back at the bottom left. FAILED: Reaching the top of the board did not clear the level. The boat returned to the start. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the top edge of the screen. CONTROLS: Clicking plants opens water channels. The boat floats upward through open water and moves horizontally on the surface.

ESTABLISHED: The timer decrements with every action and triggers a reset at zero. FAILED: Moving the player to the target without carrying a box does not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the exit square or filling a single tunnel cell. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move and turn; SPACE attaches a box on the facing side, pushes it, or drops it.

GOAL: Place three boxes into specific tunnel cells to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; Space attaches or detaches a carried box. RULE: You can only push or pull one box at a time, requiring careful path planning. TRAP: Assuming you can drop a box anywhere; placement must align perfectly with target zones.

GOAL: Guide the boat to the glowing cross by floating it through a newly dug channel. CONTROLS: Arrows steer the boat horizontally; clicking the plant clears the path to the surface. RULE: The boat rises only when aligned with an open vertical channel connecting deep water to the pool. TRAP: Thinking arrows lift the boat; they only shift its position, leaving it stuck below the soil.

GOAL: Move the sliding piece to the gray target square. CONTROLS: Clicking a spot moves the piece up to three spaces along the diagonal path. RULE: The piece only travels along the diagonal line where row plus column equals a constant. TRAP: Thinking the piece moves freely across the grid instead of staying on the single diagonal track.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while navigating around stationary turrets that block specific lanes. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one tile per press; the camera follows the player across the grid. RULE: Turrets only shoot in their indicated direction; they do not move or rotate during the level. TRAP: Assuming turrets slide when you enter their line of sight causes unnecessary detours; they remain fixed.

GOAL: Set each slot to the exact glyph orientation shown in the rule, not the standard alphabet shape. CONTROLS: Arrows cycle the glyph in the selected slot through seven specific orientations. RULE: The target is the precise rotated form displayed in the yellow rule row, ignoring canonical letter shapes. TRAP: Assuming the correct answer is the upright letter version wastes moves; the cycle includes specific rotated variants.

GOAL: Guide the piece down the shaft to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piece; SPACE rotates its orientation. RULE: The piece only slides in a straight line until it hits a wall or obstacle. TRAP: Assuming the piece stops mid-slide or that rotation happens instantly without confirming the new direction.

GOAL: Decode hidden patterns to fill seven output slots correctly. CONTROLS: Arrows move selection; Up cycles glyph values in a slot. RULE: Match bottom row segments to rule patterns to derive specific blue glyph sequences. TRAP: Assuming all slots share the same glyph cycle order wastes actions; verify each slot's unique mapping.

GOAL: Fill the bottom slots left to right to match the colored sequence shown at the top of the screen. CONTROLS: Click a color in the bottom palette to select it, then click an empty slot to place that color inside. RULE: Placing a color removes it from the palette, so you must arrange the remaining colors to match the target order. TRAP: Assuming a single click places the color; it actually selects the color first, requiring a second click on the slot to commit the move.

GOAL: Guide the falling block to the target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; spacebar drops it instantly. RULE: The block leaves a permanent trail that blocks future paths. TRAP: Believing the block vanishes after landing; it actually paints the path, blocking your next moves.

GOAL: Map the bottom row of seven sky symbols to yellow symbols. CONTROLS: Use arrows to cycle each yellow slot through its possible shapes. RULE: Each sky symbol links to a pink one, which then links to a yellow one. TRAP: Assuming direct sky-to-yellow mappings; you must follow the two-step pink bridge.

GOAL: Place two crosses so their arms cover all scattered dots without overlap. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected cross three spaces. Space switches between the yellow and blue crosses. RULE: Each cross has a fixed arm length. The center must be positioned so every dot falls exactly within these arm limits. TRAP: Assuming one press equals one space. Presses move three spaces, so calculating single-cell steps wastes time and exceeds the action budget.

GOAL: Navigate the 9x9 grid to the exit while avoiding red lunges and orange paths. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one tile per step. RULE: Red enemies lunge forward if you stand in their line of sight; stay clear. TRAP: Misreading grid indices caused false collisions; verify tile colors before trusting pathfinding data.

GOAL: Slide three shapes into matching outline targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space cycles through them. RULE: Shapes slide exactly three grid cells per arrow press. TRAP: Overlapping shapes is allowed, so don't waste moves avoiding collisions.

GOAL: Slide the plunger head left to touch the handle, completing the circuit. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to move the head; other inputs were unnecessary distractions. RULE: The head moves two columns left per arrow press, regardless of its size. TRAP: Believing you must fill the grid pattern to advance, wasting actions on clicks instead of simple slides.

GOAL: Merge two scattered pieces into a single larger shape by clicking a central point. CONTROLS: Clicking empty space pulls every piece on the board toward that spot simultaneously. RULE: When two identical pieces occupy the same space, they fuse into the next size up. TRAP: Do not assume you can move pieces individually; every click affects all pieces at once.

GOAL: Move three shapes to cover eight scattered dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space cycles to the next shape. RULE: Shapes move in jumps of three, so align centers to multiples of three for efficient positioning. TRAP: Assuming the horizontal line has unequal arms wastes time; it is symmetric, requiring balanced center placement.

GOAL: Fit the head through the narrow collar to escape the level. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the head; clicking the grid shrank it. RULE: The head must be two units wide to pass the gap. TRAP: Trying to squeeze the full-sized head through the blocked channel.

GOAL: Rearrange colored items so their sequence matches a hidden target pattern. CONTROLS: Click items to move them between slots and a temporary holding area; press space to submit the arrangement. RULE: The game highlights the first incorrect position, revealing the true order one step at a time. TRAP: Assuming the visible order matches the solution without verifying the hidden target sequence caused unnecessary trial and error.

GOAL: Place the magenta bead exactly at the dashed ring's center. CONTROLS: Clicking a bead moves it; clicking the gray anchor swaps its position with the moving bead. RULE: The chain line is ignored; only the magenta bead’s final position must align with the ring’s center point. TRAP: Assuming the white bead or the chain line needed to align with the ring wasted time on invalid positioning.

GOAL: Place seven colors into nested boxes following a specific reading sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette colors, then click empty slots to place them. Press space to finish. RULE: Nested boxes replace their parent slot in reading order, expanding the sequence left to right. TRAP: Assuming all slots are independent. Ignoring nesting caused misplaced colors and wasted moves.

GOAL: Move the plus cross to the orange zone and back to cover the dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the selected shape; Space switches active shape. RULE: A shape only registers when it physically overlaps the matching color zone. TRAP: Assuming the plus could cover orange dots while staying near the center; it had to travel far to reach them.

GOAL: Move two pieces to distant orbs and merge them. CONTROLS: Clicking moves the active piece toward the spot if within range. RULE: Pieces travel in straight lines until stopped by a wall or target. TRAP: Assuming one click moves a piece all the way to the orb; long distances require multiple hops.

ESTABLISHED: The blue block is immovable at the right edge. FAILED: Pushing the green block into the blue does nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Moving the blue block right. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player and push blocks; RIGHT extends the beam; UNDO reverses actions.

GOAL: Place the marker to align pre-set tiles with the target pattern. CONTROLS: Click items to select, click slots to place, space to confirm. RULE: The marker position dictates which sequence index the first green tile occupies. TRAP: Assuming green tiles always start at the first slot; they shift based on the marker's location in the red row.

ESTABLISHED: The level has a strict action budget. The goal is to land a dot on a central plus sign. FAILED: Exceeding the action limit causes failure. Solving only one color axis does not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply extending bars to maximum length without precision. CONTROLS: Clicking specific buttons extends yellow or green bars by fixed steps.

GOAL: Align the moving dots from two growing bars to hit the center target. CONTROLS: Click yellow and green buttons to extend their respective bars by fixed steps. RULE: The level completes only when both dots land exactly on the intersection point. TRAP: Clicking too many times overshoots the target, wasting your limited action budget.

GOAL: Fill the sequence with correct colors using markers to define repeating patterns. CONTROLS: Drag colors from the palette to empty slots and place markers to set boundaries. RULE: Markers split the row into segments; the pattern must repeat consistently across these defined zones. TRAP: Assuming all red slots need unique colors, when markers actually allow shared or repeated values in specific positions.

GOAL: Guide the segmented head to the exit using limited moves. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the entire snake one cell in that direction. RULE: The body follows the head’s exact path, leaving a gray trail. TRAP: Believing the push mechanic from earlier levels applies here; it does not.

GOAL: Place the correct colored items into the three boxes based on the color sequence shown in the top red box. CONTROLS: Click a color in the bottom palette to select it, then click an empty slot in a box to place it. RULE: The top box’s marker colors dictate which specific color fills the corresponding box below it. TRAP: Believing all boxes need the same set of colors; each box actually requires a unique pair matching its label.

GOAL: Arrange the ring blocks to match the target color sequence. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to rotate the ring clockwise; click the green arrow to rotate it counter-clockwise. RULE: Each rotation shifts every block one position; the sequence must align exactly with the goal pattern. TRAP: Assuming arrows only rotate one way wastes moves; testing both directions reveals they offer independent control.

GOAL: Move three shapes to cover all matching colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space cycles to the next shape. RULE: Shapes must land on target dots to change color and complete the level. TRAP: Moving all shapes before checking color changes wastes actions; verify each placement immediately.

GOAL: Reduce the scattered pieces to a single survivor. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then click the highlighted landing spot to jump. RULE: Jumps must leap directly over an adjacent piece into an empty space, removing the jumped piece. TRAP: Wasting moves on unnecessary captures early on makes the final reduction impossible.
